body: I looked into this, and while it looks like a bug, respecting background's margins is not really useful. As you can see in your mock-up, you will end up with the tabs floating in empty space. I think you are supposed to modify the `tab` styles, their margins are properly respected. It will also make the tabs fit the whole height.

I thought that respecting the margins was useful to mimic a HBox of a button group (essentially what the BottomPanel currently is) using the TabContainer backend and inheritance. It allows for the margins to be a guarantee and automatically add a margin to any other controls in the tabbar region (say if you wanted to implement https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/2250). Personally I would find it very useful but I'm open to hearing what you think. Admittedly the example above is exaggerated for effect, in practice the margin would probably be under 8 pixels and the tabs would have separation between each other. Note that current theming of TabContainer only allows for custom margins on the left or (both top and bottom using extended margins, otherwise the menu popup icon would not be vertically centered). Custom margins for the right (moving the popup menu icon) and separate margins for the top and bottom are impractical/impossible right now. This fix would also allow users to place their own custom controls over the TabBar that are respected by the tabs (ie not intersecting), although they would have to input the size of their controls. This is a more realistic example of how it would look (using the attached PR), the highlights are there to show the boundaries of the tabs. In the meantime I'll try and see if I can do something using negative extended margins.
